tasks.short: Administer reward, performance, safety and employee recreation programmes, resolving exceptions and monitoring delivery.

steps.what: Review programme rules, policy changes, deadlines and outstanding issues.
Approve programme changes and budgets after required consultation.
Apply approved compensation parameters and validate their effective dates.
Maintain benefits enrolments against employee choices and eligibility rules.
Resolve pay and benefit exceptions within delegated authority.
Launch performance reviews, assign forms and chase outstanding submissions.
Facilitate calibration and resolve disputed performance assessments.
Assign safety-programme actions and track completion with the safety officer.
Arrange employee activity invitations and collect registrations.
Reconcile programme costs, participation, exceptions and completion reports.
Review programme outcomes and choose corrective proposals.

tasks.design: Configure eligibility, effective dates and review cycles in the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {TALENT}; use the {WORKFLOW} for safety actions and activity registrations. Deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feeds the {BI}, while pay configuration, reward exceptions and performance calibration retain specific human approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each programme has different owners, dates and rules. A spreadsheet often ties together otherwise capable systems, while unusual cases interrupt routine administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Most routine work can use existing configuration. AI-assisted coding makes shared validation rules, reports and missing integrations cheaper to deliver without adding a model to every step.
tasks.still_hard: Fair reward exceptions and performance disputes require accountable judgement. Changes to pay, appraisal, staff-data use or monitoring may require consultation or consent under national rules; specialist safety responsibilities remain.
tasks.human_edge: Explain difficult decisions, recognise unequal effects and mediate between consistent rules and legitimate individual circumstances.

ambition.what: Weekly reward-exception review before the payroll cut-off.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager works from a consolidated exception queue and spends more time on reward fairness, calibration and programme outcomes. Existing budget, pay and performance decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review reward exceptions for consistency across comparable roles.
reach.learn: Reward governance, effective dating and internal-equity analysis.

reach.task: Validate approved compensation changes before payroll processing.
reach.learn: Payroll cut-offs, reconciliation controls and correction procedures.

reach.task: Track safety-training completion and route overdue requirements.
reach.learn: Certification evidence, renewal rules and escalation boundaries.

Review pay validation reports and resolve eligibility exceptions.
Monitor integration failures, duplicate changes and missed deadlines.
Review aggregate programme outcomes and avoid treating participation as an employee performance measure.

tasks.short: Identify vacancies, recruit candidates, conduct interviews and agree hiring decisions.

steps.what: Compare staffing needs with occupied positions and approved headcount.
Approve the vacancy, budget and hiring priority.
Prepare the role description, advert and interview criteria with the hiring manager.

loop.input: Approved vacancy, role template, pay range and hiring-manager notes.
loop.output: Draft vacancy pack with traceable requirements and interview questions.
loop.check: Check required fields, pay range and unsupported requirements; hiring manager checks relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved requirements return to the recruiter.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover structure; role-specific wording requires interpreting free-text notes.

steps.what: Approve and publish the vacancy.
Read applications and assemble evidence against the agreed criteria.

loop.input: Candidate application and explicit vacancy criteria.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence grid, with missing evidence marked unknown.
loop.check: Validate quotations and source locations; recruiter checks omissions and unsupported inferences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per application; unreadable material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applications contain varied free text; fixed fields miss relevant evidence.

steps.what: Choose the interview shortlist using applications and documented criteria.
Arrange interviews and send candidate instructions.
Interview candidates, answer questions and record evidence.
Select the preferred candidate and document the reasons.
Prepare the offer using approved terms and contract templates.
Approve the offer and release it for signature.
Record the accepted offer and pass starter details to HR administration.

tasks.design: Configure vacancy approvals, interview booking, offer templates and starter transfer across the {ATS}, {CALENDAR}, {ESIGN} and {HCM}. Bounded loops draft vacancy packs and extract source-linked application evidence; people shortlist, interview, select and approve offers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful recruitment features often exist, but inconsistent role criteria and disconnected approvals leave manual coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building missing connectors and constrained document helpers.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing potential, providing accommodations and making fair comparisons remain demanding. GDPR and EU AI Act assessment, meaningful human oversight and consultation under applicable national rules remain necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Build candidate trust, test evidence through conversation and judge trade-offs that a formal criterion cannot settle.

ambition.what: Fortnightly vacancy-priority review against approved headcount and hiring capacity.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time chasing bookings and assembling paperwork, and more time challenging vacancy priorities and interview quality. Headcount, selection and offer approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design structured interview criteria and candidate evidence forms.
reach.learn: Job analysis, accessible assessment and evidence-based interview design.

reach.task: Validate vacancy pay ranges before publication.
reach.learn: Pay structures, internal equity and the applicable national transparency rules.

Handle scheduling exceptions and candidate accommodation requests.
Maintain templates, permissions, retention rules and connector mappings.
Sample omissions and inconsistent treatment, including effects on different candidate groups.
tasks.statement: Identify staff vacancies and recruit, interview, and select applicants.

tasks.short: Match employees to team and project needs while balancing capacity, capability, preferences, and fairness.

steps.what: Collect team or project staffing needs, required capabilities, dates, and priorities.
Check employee availability, current assignments, working patterns, and verified qualifications.
Build feasible staffing options and flag capacity conflicts or missing qualifications.
Discuss staffing options, employee preferences, workload, development goals, and team relationships.
Resolve competing demands and approve an allocation within agreed staffing authority.
Update approved assignments and effective dates in employee and project records.
Send confirmed assignment details to affected employees and managers.

tasks.design: Capture staffing requirements in {PROJECT} and join capacity and verified qualification records from the {HCM} and {LMS}. Deterministic constraint checks show feasible options in {BI}; people discuss suitability and approve allocations before integrations update records and {WORKFLOW} sends confirmations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, qualifications, and assignments lived in separate records. Informal negotiations and stale capacity data made automated allocation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared assignment register and deterministic constraint checks can remove repeated reconciliation. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of connectors and scenario views without introducing automated suitability scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Actual capacity changes quickly. Team dynamics, employee aspirations, contractual changes, and competing managerial priorities need negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Balance development opportunities, employee wishes, operational pressure, and fairness without reducing people to scores.

ambition.what: Fortnightly cross-team capacity review before staffing conflicts become urgent.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less capacity reconciliation and record updating, with more time for employee discussions and contested allocations. An agreed cross-team mandate can let the HR manager resolve routine resource conflicts; permanent employment changes retain their existing approval route.

reach.task: Coordinate internal moves and verify assignment conditions.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, qualification evidence, internal mobility processes, and employee consultation.

Managers and employees supply structured requirements and preferences.
Feasibility checks use explicit constraints and do not infer personality or predict employee performance.

Maintain explicit feasibility constraints and effective dates.
Review exceptions and document reasons for contested allocations.
Monitor access to development opportunities.
Handle failed updates and notifications without duplicating assignments.
tasks.statement: Allocate human resources, ensuring appropriate matches between personnel.

tasks.short: Explain policies, job conditions, pay, progression, and benefits to employees and candidates.

steps.what: Receive the question and establish the employee or candidate context.
Find current policies, benefit terms, and job information in the {DOCS}.
Check authorised personal eligibility and employment terms in the {HCM}.
Draft an explanation linking the question to applicable policy and eligibility facts.

loop.input: HR inquiry, approved policy passages, and minimum authorised eligibility facts.
loop.output: HR answer draft with passage citations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate cited passages, policy versions, and eligibility fields; an HR specialist checks applicability before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair; missing, conflicting, or unsupported terms route to an HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions. Novel free-text questions spanning several policies need a bounded drafting loop.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive circumstances, policy ambiguity, or progression expectations with the requester.
Check and send the written answer, recording any follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure an inquiry queue in {HELPDESK} and searchable, versioned policy references in {DOCS}, with authorised eligibility lookups from {HCM}. Approved FAQ answers use templates; a bounded loop drafts unusual answers with citations for HR review before sending through {EMAIL}. Sensitive questions retain a direct conversation and a visible route to an HR specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were scattered, ownership was unclear, and personalised answers required checking several sources. Search alone did not explain how terms applied to a particular question.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned knowledge articles and structured eligibility checks support reliable retrieval. A small drafting loop can reduce writing effort once source quality and access are settled.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies, collective agreements, personal circumstances, and implied promises about pay or promotion need human interpretation. Keeping source material current remains ongoing work.
tasks.human_edge: HR recognises the concern behind the question and explains difficult limits without losing trust.

ambition.what: Provide shift workers with an out-of-hours policy reference service and a tracked human callback.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated searches and more complex advice and follow-up. HR gains a clearer view of recurring policy confusion, while authority to grant exceptions stays unchanged.

reach.task: Explain benefit eligibility and job-level criteria.
reach.learn: Benefit exclusions, job-evaluation criteria, and when a written answer could create an unintended commitment.

reach.task: Interpret a disputed employment policy.
reach.learn: Collective-agreement precedence, escalation thresholds, and national employment rules.

tasks.short: Handle staffing shortages, disputes, disciplinary cases, and dismissals through evidence, fair procedure, and difficult conversations.

steps.what: Receive the staffing problem and establish urgency and procedural route.
Gather relevant records and reconstruct events or staffing constraints.

loop.input: Selected case documents and correspondence with source identifiers.
loop.output: Draft chronology separating recorded events, allegations, and missing evidence.
loop.check: Validate source identifiers and dates; HR checks omissions, contradictions, and allegation labels.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved contradictions remain visible for human investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured records support direct assembly, but relevant events often appear in narrative correspondence.

steps.what: Hear employees and managers and test disputed facts or staffing needs.
Choose a proportionate staffing, mediation, disciplinary, or dismissal response.
Review procedure and approve the proposed employment action under delegated authority.
Prepare the action letter or written resolution from the approved decision.
Explain the decision, deliver written terms, and discuss practical next steps.
Update authorised records and initiate required staffing or exit follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure restricted case routes and procedural checklists in the {WORKFLOW}, with authorised evidence from the {HCM} and {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares a cited chronology, and deterministic templates prepare letters from approved decision fields. People investigate, decide, approve, and deliver employment actions; approved records trigger the appropriate follow-up in the {HCM} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was dispersed, procedures varied by case, and the consequences made broad automation unsuitable. Much of the work was already human judgement rather than administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations, chronology checks, and template generators are cheaper to build with coding assistance. Narrative extraction can assist preparation while leaving decisions with people.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, proportionality, legal procedure, staffing alternatives, and emotional consequences remain difficult. Unrecorded events cannot be reconstructed reliably by software.
tasks.human_edge: Hear conflicting accounts fairly, recognise power imbalances, and take responsibility for consequential decisions.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and paperwork leaves more time for interviews, mediation, and exploring staffing alternatives. Disciplinary and dismissal authority does not change.

reach.task: Check disciplinary procedure and advise on settlement options.
reach.learn: National procedure, collective agreements, proportionality, and evidence standards.

reach.task: Develop redeployment options for staffing shortages.
reach.learn: Skill matching, contractual constraints, and consultation requirements.

evidence.claim: Case checklists, approved-decision templates, and authorised record updates can use configuration and deterministic code.
Narrative chronology extraction needs review and does not establish truth, credibility, or an appropriate employment outcome.

tasks.short: Advise managers on employment policies and recommend policy changes.

steps.what: Receive a manager's query and open a confidential case.
Clarify facts, immediate concerns and the manager's intended action.
Find relevant policies, guidance and earlier approved advice.
Assess the case and prepare advice or a policy change recommendation.

loop.input: Minimised case facts and applicable approved policies and legal guidance.
loop.output: Draft advice separating sourced requirements, options, missing facts and proposed policy changes.
loop.check: Validate citations and versions; HR manager checks reasoning, proportionality and need for legal advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported conclusions or conflicting guidance go to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text facts must be related to policies with context-dependent exceptions.

steps.what: Explain advice, challenge assumptions and agree appropriate next steps.
Review proposed policy changes and authorise required consultation or adoption.
Publish approved policy versions and update guidance links.

tasks.design: Configure confidential intake in the {HELPDESK} and versioned policy retrieval from the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts cited advice for HR review; the {WORKFLOW} publishes policy changes only after the required consultation and approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on sensitive facts, local rules and policy versions. Shared inboxes preserve conversations but make precedents and access controls difficult to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Case permissions, versioned search and approval workflows already cover the records work. A bounded model can prepare a sourced first draft from approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Harassment, discrimination and conflicting accounts require careful fact finding and independent judgement. GDPR applies to case data; national rules govern employment procedures and consultation, while the EU AI Act requires assessment if scope expands into employment decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice fear, retaliation risk or missing context, and challenge a manager without closing down disclosure.

ambition.what: Monthly review of recurring policy exceptions

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time finding policy text and drafting routine explanations, leaving more time for sensitive conversations and recurring problems. They can propose policy priorities from case patterns; formal policy and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review recurring policy exceptions for unequal treatment.
reach.learn: Evidence standards, protected characteristics, confidentiality and the limits of small-group comparisons.

tasks.short: Analyse compensation and benefits, then propose competitive and compliant policy changes.

steps.what: Export workforce, pay and benefit records for the review.
Reconcile population, pay definitions and employer costs.
Compare job scope and reward levels with relevant market benchmarks.

loop.input: Job descriptions, benchmark role definitions and an approved comparison rubric.
loop.output: Proposed benchmark matches with cited scope differences and explicit unmatched jobs.
loop.check: Validate benchmark identifiers; compensation specialist confirms scope, seniority and each accepted match.
loop.stop: One proposal and one correction pass per job; ambiguous jobs remain unmatched for specialist evaluation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Job titles and free-text responsibilities do not provide reliable exact matches.

steps.what: Model pay ranges, benefit options, distributional effects and budget trade-offs.
Check options against applicable law, collective agreements and benefit terms.
Draft proposed policy wording and explain the recommended option.

loop.input: Selected scenario, current policy and reviewed compliance advice.
loop.output: Policy redline and explanation tied to scenario identifiers.
loop.check: Compare every amount and eligibility condition with scenario fields; HR checks wording against legal advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved terms remain flagged for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy explanations and amendments vary with the selected trade-offs and existing wording.

steps.what: Discuss the proposal with employee representatives and record their response.
Approve the policy, budget and effective date after required consultation.
Publish the approved policy and retain its decision history.

tasks.design: Connect the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {ERP} to a governed baseline in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then calculate reward scenarios with deterministic rules and expose comparisons in the {BI}. tasks.previous_blocker: Pay definitions, job descriptions and purchased benchmarks rarely align cleanly. Scenario work becomes expensive when each review rebuilds mappings and reconciliations.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings and calculation code cover the numerical work. Bounded models can compare job descriptions and draft explanations, with specialists checking their outputs.
tasks.still_hard: Market data licensing, comparable job scope and unexplained pay differences remain expensive. GDPR, the EU AI Act where applicable, collective agreements and national rules constrain data use, evaluation and policy adoption.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible trade-offs between competitiveness, fairness, affordability and employee expectations.

tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time reconciling files and rebuilding scenarios, and more time challenging job matches and reward trade-offs. They can recommend targeted budget changes more frequently; authority to set budgets or change individual pay still requires an explicit mandate.

tasks.short: Plan and deliver new employee orientation.

steps.what: Check incoming starters, roles, locations and start dates.
Arrange sessions, speakers and invitations.
Assemble role and location materials from the standard orientation content.
Welcome starters, explain organisational objectives and discuss their questions.
Introduce team priorities and connect starters with colleagues.
Record attendance and send outstanding learning and follow-up reminders.
Review starter feedback and choose changes for the next cohort.

tasks.previous_blocker: Starter changes, speaker availability and content variants require coordination across systems. Small cohorts made bespoke integration difficult to justify.

tasks.short: Answer employee questions, interpret agreements, and help management and employees resolve workplace problems.

steps.what: Receive questions and identify urgent, sensitive, or routine cases.
Find employee records, applicable contracts, policies, and previous correspondence.
Interpret relevant clauses and prepare a response or escalation.

loop.input: Employee question and authorised contract and policy passages, including versions and effective dates.
loop.output: Draft response with clause references, uncertainties, and suggested escalation.
loop.check: Verify references and dates mechanically; HR checks applicability and interpretation before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; missing, conflicting, or inapplicable sources return to HR.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed answers cover common questions; ambiguous questions and varied contract wording need contextual reading.

steps.what: Discuss the issue with employees and managers and hear their concerns.

Draft agreed wording and identify unresolved clauses.

Interpret applicable agreement clauses for a specific employee case.

reach.task: Prepare clause comparisons and bargaining impact assessments.

tasks.short: Forecast workforce supply, demand, costs, and hiring needs.

steps.what: Export employee, vacancy, absence, and pay baselines.
Supply approved budgets, workload forecasts, and cost assumptions.
Agree demand drivers, productivity assumptions, and plausible organisational changes with department managers.
Reconcile positions, working hours, cost centres, and conflicting snapshots.
Calculate workforce gaps, hiring dates, and costs under alternative assumptions.
Prepare the workforce proposal with recommended actions and unresolved trade-offs.
Challenge assumptions and approve workforce priorities and spending limits.

A deterministic scenario calculator feeds a {BI} view and a proposal template in {DOCS}; managers supply assumptions, choose recommendations, and approve spending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different snapshots, inconsistent position identifiers, and local planning workbooks made repeatable calculations expensive to maintain. Demand assumptions still required management judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build adapters, reconciliation rules, scenario calculations, and document templates. No new forecasting breakthrough is assumed.

tasks.human_edge: The manager understands which shortages threaten delivery and negotiates credible trade-offs between hiring, redeployment, training, and workload.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on the timing of critical-role recruitment.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding forecasts and more time testing department assumptions. Within delegated budget limits, they can bring forward recruitment decisions using current scenarios.

reach.task: Model the cost of alternative workforce mixes.
reach.learn: Salary structures, employer costs, and cost sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: Structured workforce data supports deterministic reconciliation, scenario calculations, and templated reporting.
A study across 11 occupations including HR found modest average time savings; it does not validate these step estimates.

Maintain cost assumptions, workload drivers, and scenario formulas.
Compare forecasts with actual outcomes and investigate persistent errors.

tasks.statement: Prepare personnel forecast to project employment needs.

tasks.short: Prepare the HR operating budget, agree spending priorities, and monitor costs against the approved plan.

steps.what: Retrieve HR spending and commitments from the {ERP}.
Collect staffing, recruitment, training, and supplier spending proposals.
Calculate baseline costs and alternative spending scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Negotiate service priorities and affordable spending with the finance team and department managers.
Approve the HR budget and spending limits.
Record approved budget lines and limits in the {ERP}.
Compare actual spending with budget and decide corrective action.

tasks.design: Use {WORKFLOW} forms to collect proposals and a scheduled {DATA_PLATFORM} job to join approved inputs with {ERP} actuals. Deterministic calculations generate scenarios and a {BI} variance dashboard; approval precedes budget posting to the {ERP}. The HR manager negotiates priorities and recommends corrective action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, proposal formats, and planning assumptions differed across teams. Existing reporting often covered actuals without commitments or service demand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and reporting can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mappings, scenario calculations, and validation checks; no model loop is required.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing affordable service levels and estimating recruitment or training demand remain uncertain. Poor commitment data can make an apparently precise forecast misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The HR manager explains the consequences of cuts and negotiates tradeoffs between employee needs and available funds.

ambition.what: Monthly recruitment-versus-training spending recommendations using current commitments.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less consolidation and more discussion of service demand and spending choices. Budget approval rights stay unchanged; any delegated reallocation limit needs agreement with the finance director.

reach.task: Cost a training plan against delivery capacity.
reach.learn: Course unit costs, attendance assumptions, and how training outcomes support investment choices.

reach.task: Estimate the cost of proposed benefit changes.
reach.learn: Eligibility rules, employer contributions, and uncertainty in employee uptake.

evidence.claim: Structured budget inputs support deterministic scenario calculations and variance reporting; the proposed scope and effort are estimates.
Observed chatbot adoption does not establish large reductions in HR working hours.

Step shares and remaining time are estimates for a mid-size European company, not measured savings.
Existing reporting and form capabilities are used before custom code.

Resolve missing commitments and late proposals.
Review scenario totals and unexpected variances.
Monitor imports and prevent duplicate budget postings.
tasks.statement: Prepare and follow budgets for personnel operations.

tasks.short: Develop, administer, and evaluate job-relevant applicant tests.

steps.what: Define job requirements, assessment purpose, and candidate accommodation needs with the hiring manager.
Select validated tests or develop job-relevant work samples and scoring rubrics.
Validate and approve the protocol using specialist review and evidence from the assessment platform {OTHER}.
Invite candidates through the assessment platform {OTHER} and explain timing, purpose, and support.
Monitor completion and resolve access problems and accommodation requests.
Consolidate objective scores and flag incomplete or irregular test records.
Interpret results, assess subjective responses, and approve a contextual assessment report.
Evaluate reliability, candidate experience, outcomes, and lawful group-level disparity measures.
Approve continued use, specialist revalidation, revision, or withdrawal of the assessment.

tasks.design: Configure invitations, reminders, completion records, and validated objective scoring in the assessment platform {OTHER}, linked to the {ATS}. Deterministic reporting in {BI} supports periodic evaluation with restricted access and minimum group sizes. Qualified people approve protocols, interpret results, and handle accommodations; hiring decisions remain with authorised people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Administration crossed the {ATS}, an assessment platform {OTHER}, and local reports. Test validity and interpretation required specialist expertise that automation could not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheaper integration work can connect existing validated assessments, candidate support queues, and evaluation reports. Configuration handles routine administration without introducing model-based candidate scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Small hiring volumes limit statistical evaluation. Accessibility, test validity, changing job requirements, and interpreting individual results require specialist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Qualified people judge whether a test measures relevant capability and whether a candidate's circumstances make the result misleading.

ambition.what: A quarterly assessment-quality review covering validity, accommodations, and candidate experience.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time coordinating tests and more time checking their usefulness and fairness. They gain a clearer basis to suspend a poor assessment within existing authority.

reach.task: Review assessment accessibility and investigate disparities in selection outcomes.
reach.learn: Lawful group analysis, reasonable accommodations, statistical uncertainty, and complaint handling.

AI used to evaluate candidates falls within the employment uses listed in AI Act Annex III; deterministic administration alone does not establish that classification.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, including relevant employment decisions.
Reported hiring-AI litigation illustrates that employers retain responsibilities when procuring screening technology.

An internal or external qualified assessment specialist supports the HR manager.
The initial implementation uses existing validated tests or work samples; new psychometric validation is outside the build estimate.
Candidate test-taking time is excluded from staff-effort shares.
The system does not automatically reject, rank, or select candidates.
Objective scoring uses the approved rubric; subjective interpretation remains human.
GDPR applies throughout; consultation and employment requirements depend on national rules.

Handle delivery failures, incomplete records, and accommodation requests.
Review evaluation dashboards with a qualified specialist.
Investigate complaints and unexplained outcome differences.

tasks.statement: Develop, administer, and evaluate applicant tests.

tasks.short: Oversee job evaluation and classification, calibrate ratings, and approve defensible position grades.

steps.what: Request current job profiles and identify positions due for evaluation.
Confirm the position's duties, scope, reporting relationships, and required expertise.
Extract evidence against evaluation factors and identify missing or contradictory information.

loop.input: Confirmed job profile and versioned evaluation factor definitions.
loop.output: Factor evidence table with exact source passages and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Validate source references automatically; evaluator checks relevance and rejects inferred responsibilities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per profile; missing evidence returns to the department manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Responsibilities appear in varied prose. Keyword rules cannot reliably map context to evaluation factors.

steps.what: Choose factor ratings and calculate the proposed grade under the evaluation framework.
Calibrate proposed ratings against comparable positions and resolve contested factor interpretations.
Approve the classification and its documented rationale or return it for reconsideration.
Record the approved classification and effective date in the position register.

tasks.design: Use structured profile reviews in the {HCM} or {WORKFLOW}, with a bounded loop extracting cited factor evidence from {DOCS}. Deterministic calculations and comparator views support evaluator ratings; approved classifications write back to the {HCM} with framework versions and an audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arithmetic was already easy to automate. Profile quality, framework interpretation, disputed comparators, and disconnected approval records limited broader automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can prepare evidence tables from varied profiles. AI-assisted coding can make the surrounding records, calculation, and integration work cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Framework interpretation, unequal descriptions of comparable work, appeals, and proprietary evaluation methods still require expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize inflated or understated responsibilities, challenge biased comparators, and explain a defensible rating.

ambition.what: Role-change impact review before a proposed reorganisation receives final approval.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing profiles and copying evidence toward calibration and contested cases. With an explicit mandate, the HR manager can require evaluation evidence before role changes are approved.

tasks.short: Track employment law, arbitration, and collective agreements to assess trends and organisational implications.

steps.what: Collect relevant legal updates, arbitration decisions, and collective agreement versions.
Read sources and record changes, dates, affected topics, and recurring industry themes.

loop.input: Versioned source documents and the previous change register.
loop.output: Proposed change entries with quotations, source locations, jurisdiction, legal status, dates, and uncertainty.
loop.check: Validate source locations and dates mechanically; the manager checks cited passages and distinctions between proposals and effective rules.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; missing passages, conflicting dates, or unreadable pages go to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document retrieval and version comparison are deterministic; identifying relevant changes across varied legal prose needs bounded language interpretation.

steps.what: Assess applicability, industry patterns, and implications for employment policies.
Resolve material ambiguities and confirm interpretations that would change employment practice.
Approve a briefing containing trends, implications, actions, and source references.
Distribute the approved briefing and archive superseded material.

A bounded extraction loop proposes cited change entries, while deterministic templates assemble the briefing from reviewed entries and confirmed interpretations. Configured approval and distribution in {WORKFLOW} publish only approved material.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used inconsistent formats, and legal changes required interpretation across documents and versions. Generic search alerts could identify documents but could not establish their local implications.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can produce source-linked drafts from varied documents. Faster integration work makes version tracking, review queues, and publication controls practical for smaller HR teams.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability depends on jurisdiction, agreement coverage, facts, and legal interpretation. Source access, publication delays, and ambiguous decisions remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes an interesting industry signal from a change that warrants advice, consultation, or action.

ambition.what: A monthly employment-change briefing for department managers with dated actions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting documents and more time interpreting implications with legal advisers. They can prioritise policy reviews, but gain no authority to settle disputed law.

reach.task: Translate collective agreement changes into operational guidance.
reach.learn: Agreement coverage, interpretive practice, and consultation procedures.

GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

tasks.short: Design, run, and evaluate HR programmes such as pay equity, childcare support, and employee awards.

steps.what: Agree the programme's purpose, target group, constraints, and success measures.
Gather the employee, pay, participation, and programme records needed for the brief.
Calculate coverage, costs, and relevant disparities under alternative programme rules.
Design programme options, eligibility criteria, safeguards, and delivery arrangements.
Consult employees, representatives, and delivery teams about proposed options.
Approve programme rules, funding, and launch conditions after required consultation.
Collect applications or nominations and prepare eligibility checks and proposed allocations.
Review exceptions and approve individual awards, benefits, or pay adjustments.
Record approved allocations and route delivery instructions to payroll or programme providers.
Evaluate participation, costs, outcomes, and complaints against the programme's aims.

tasks.human_edge: The manager designs a programme employees regard as fair, reconciles competing needs, and handles sensitive individual circumstances.

ambition.what: A childcare-support pilot accessible to shift workers.

tasks.short: Arrange outplacement or relocation support for employees leaving the company.

steps.what: Retrieve the departure case, support policy and available services.
Check contractual support entitlement, deadlines and spending limits.
Discuss the employee's priorities, circumstances and preferred support.
Prepare a support plan with services, costs, contacts and deadlines.

loop.check: Validate costs, dates and service identifiers with rules; HR checks preference fidelity and unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per case; unresolved content returns to the HR specialist.

steps.what: Approve the support plan and any funding exceptions within delegated limits.
Confirm the employee's choice and send the agreed referral details.
Coordinate the first appointment using employee and provider availability.
Check whether support started and address concerns with the employee.
Record agreed actions, delivery status and case closure.

tasks.short: Choose and contract suppliers for employee services.

Prepare a supplier request using requirements and standard terms.
Send the request to suitable suppliers and collect responses.
Compare proposal prices, coverage, service levels and exclusions.

Review contractual obligations, employee data handling and legal departures.
Approve the commercial commitment and any policy exceptions.
Sign the approved contract and obtain the supplier's signature.
Record service eligibility, contract obligations and renewal dates.
